body.heading: Notice the helpers
paragraphs: Think about the people who help your family every week. Someone cooks, someone drives, someone fixes things, someone cheers you up.
Pick one helper together. Today, your thank-you will be a drawing instead of words.

body.heading: Draw the thank-you
paragraphs: Draw the person doing the helpful thing. Draw yourself in the picture too, smiling or helping alongside.
If drawing people feels tricky, draw the thing instead: the meal, the fixed toy, the tidy room. The meaning matters more than the drawing.

body.heading: Deliver it like a surprise
paragraphs: Give your drawing to the person and tell them one sentence about it, like: “This is you making my favourite dinner. Thank you.”
Watch their face. A thank-you you can keep on the fridge lasts much longer than a thank-you that floats away.

description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: say thank you to a family helper with a drawing instead of words.
